plain: The art of speaking well in public

webster.text: The art of speaking well, or of speaking according to the rules of rhetoric, in order to persuade.

more.text: Among the Romanists, a close apartment near a bed-chamber, furnished with an altar, a crucifix, &c. for private devotions.
A place allotted for prayer, or a place for public worship.

example.quote: On so important an occasion, and before so respectable a body, I expected a new display of his powers of oratory ; but, instead of proceeding to investigate the merits of the new plan of government, the worthy character informed us of horrors which he felt, of apprehensions to his mind, which made him tremblingly fearful of the fate of the commonwealth.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 5, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
